coverage_limitation: City of Albuquerque only. Undated rows are not emitted. A generator mention is not treated as behind-the-meter, bridge, or temporary power unless the description says so. The file is a historical extract, not a live permit feed.

City limits only; literal-keyword backfill is not all data-center work. Older status changes outside the overlap or fixed backfill are not comprehensively monitored. Permit-listed names and permit-listed phones do not establish current employment or buying authority.

Not the full 664,565-row history. Closed/completed records remain evidence and are not admitted as current Signals. Applicant is not a buyer role. No construction start, project owner, temporary rental need, MW, supply gap, or authority is inferred; declared valuation and area are not power need. Status changes on records outside the recent issue window are not monitored.

Only CEQA filings; projects exempt from CEQA or filed under another development type are missed. When more documents arrive than the per-run bound, ones naming a data center only in their description can be missed. A CEQA filing is environmental review, not construction.

Chicago status monitoring uses the official Socrata :updated_at row timestamp with a two-day overlap. Longer outages can miss changes; a dataset-wide replacement may exceed the bounded row limit and will fail visibly. Express Electrical Work includes small and residential work; inclusion in collection does not guarantee Signal admission. No dedicated procurement or commissioning coverage.

As retrieved 2026-10-01, linked June-August 2026 workbooks contain 95 commercial rows / 89 unique Record IDs after six repeated IDs; issue dates span 2026-06-01 through 2026-08-28. Five use descriptions indicate residential occupancy despite the source Record Type being Commercial and are rejected by admission. Monthly publication lag leaves recent coverage incomplete. Does not cover all permits, alterations, or electrical permits, or prove current work, temporary-power need, load, rental demand, or authority.

As retrieved 2026-10-01 15:44Z, layer count 11,391; 90-day issue query returned 68 features / 67 unique permit IDs, dates 2026-08-04 through 2026-09-29; all 68 raw B1_APPL_ST values were blank. NewCommercial only, not citywide electrical coverage or all alterations. B1_APPL_ST is retained verbatim; one-character Status is geocoding status, not lifecycle. 60-day freshness bound. An issue event does not prove current work, rental need, load, fuel fit, or authority.

City of Fort Worth permits only; neighboring cities and county permits are not covered. Projects that never use the words data center in the permit text are missed. Filed permits may be incomplete submittals; job value is the applicant's estimate.

Not a complete air-application registry. Current application-link fields are empty; full applications may require agency request. Public notices are references only. At most 24 generator excerpts per PDF, 8 general pages; bounds and omitted excerpt counts are retained. Installed standby ratings are not rental demand.

The CCC open-data catalog states that published data is self-reported and has no completeness, accuracy, or timeliness guarantee. Snapshot and application dates are retained separately. Only dated pending/reopened records with applicant and physical Massachusetts site may enter ordinary Signals; application status does not prove construction, current work, operations, load, rental demand, a buyer, or authority.
The public-review index is not the full DEQ permit inventory. Detail pages are not fetched. Rows without a comment-window date stay undated. OCC utility dockets are not in this source.
City of San Antonio permits only; unincorporated Bexar County and other cities are not covered. Projects whose permit name never says data center are missed. Valuation is the applicant's estimate.

Seattle exposes no per-row status-change date; Socrata :updated_at was refreshed across 193257 rows in the same recent interval, so it is not a reliable row-change signal. Older permit status edits are not monitored by this discovery query. Remedy: add a bounded worker query for previously retained active permit IDs or a source lifecycle feed.

This is a generation-injection queue, not a large-load or data-center queue. Wind, solar, and storage-only requests are not emitted. Capacity is interconnection MW, not site load. SPP does not publish a separate large-load queue here.
Bounded rolling Taylor CivicPlus Development News/Notices categories 30/31 archive lookback with configured overlap; no atomic upstream snapshot is available.

On October 23, 2026 the hub and the July and August TAC and LLWG pages did not link a newer status PDF. The July LLWG packet is a short chair update, not a project list. Chart pages in the March deck do not name projects. Stated MW totals are queue totals, not a site load.

The location is the listing's Location column, rendered with Texas because the listing is the state's JETI register. A row with no Date Announced has no event date. Capital investment is the figure the listing prints. It is not an inferred load.

The table names an applicant and a school district. It does not name a street, city, or county, so rows are not assigned a Texas site. Posted PDFs are linked and are not downloaded. The API lastUpdated field can lag the row dates.

A certificate-of-convenience search returns more than 1,800 historical electric dockets and is not ingested. These rows are docket index entries. They have no file-stamp date, so they stay evidence. Filing text for 58481 and 59142 remains on texas-puct-large-load-filings.
This is the filing index, not an ERCOT large-load queue and not a site list. A filing is located only when its own text names a place. Docket membership is not treated as a Texas street address.

Not all historical Texas permits. No pending-application feed or older-month correction monitoring. Outages longer than the prior-month overlap can miss activity. Current file over four days old, missing previous-month EOM, changed framing, or bounds fail visibly. Production date, load, fuel suitability, rental demand and contacts are UNKNOWN.

Applications for exceptions only, not flaring/venting measurements. Rule 32 also permits some flaring without an exception application. Public query excludes pre-2021-05-02 online-system filings; older filings outside the three-day submittal window are not rechecked for status changes and no historical backfill is included. Application details and authorization documents are not fetched. Physical flare/vent site, requested volume, gas composition, continuous flow, generator fit, MW, rental demand, buyer, and buying authority remain UNKNOWN.

This is not every TXR150000 NOI in Texas. The result table does not state an authorization date, so no date is inferred. Site driving directions are kept in the description and are not the classified place. Expired, terminated, and pending application rows are not in this pull.

These three fixed queries are not the full NSR inventory. The existing pending-NSR listing remains a separate source. A generator or turbine row is not behind-the-meter, bridge, or temporary power unless the row text says so. Driving directions stay in the abstract; the place used for region is the near city and county.

Pending NSR case-by-case applications only; permits by rule and standard permits are not in this listing. TCEQ began moving pending-application publishing to its Permit Search Portal on August 31, 2026, so this listing may thin out. Summaries give site and purpose but rarely MW; proposed onsite generation is proposed supply, not adequate power.

Only applications still in TCEQ's public notice window. Registrations appear here briefly; earlier notices are not backfilled. The batch plant operator is a materials supplier, not the project owner or GC.

Only projects of $50,000 or more registered with TDLR, matched by project name; projects named without a data-center term are missed. Start and completion dates and cost are the registrant's estimates. Registration is accessibility review, not a building permit.
